# Minimal active-row rank and exact capacity variations

These finite-dimensional lemmas concern the stochastic-capacity problem. They do not assert that every full row has a usable positive curvature direction or settle OC.

## 1. Continuity and attained weighted maxima

For a fixed probability law Xi on the standard m-coordinate simplex and d>=1, put

    phi(x)=inf_(t>0,Pr(x dot Xi<=t)>0) t/Pr(x dot Xi<=t)^(1/d), x>=0.

This function is coordinatewise nondecreasing, positively homogeneous, and continuous on the whole nonnegative orthant. Monotonicity and homogeneity follow directly from the distribution functions (including phi(0)=0). Also phi(x)<=max_j x_j, by taking a full-capture threshold.

For continuity at x, let x^(l)->x and epsilon_l=max_j|x_j^(l)-x_j|. For every fixed t>0 with F_x(t)>0, coordinatewise monotonicity and the translation identity F_(x+epsilon 1)(t+epsilon)=F_x(t) give

    phi(x^(l)) <= (t+epsilon_l)/F_x(t)^(1/d).

Taking limsup and then the infimum over t gives limsup phi(x^(l))<=phi(x). If x has a positive entry, choose delta_l=epsilon_l/min_(x_j>0)x_j; for sufficiently large l it is less than one, and x^(l)>=(1-delta_l)x coordinatewise. Thus liminf phi(x^(l))>=phi(x). If x=0, the bound by max_j x_j^(l) proves continuity directly. No passage of a threshold through an atom has been assumed.

Consequently every nonnegative weighted sum H_c(X)=sum_i c_i phi(X_i) attains a maximum on the compact column-stochastic matrix domain. There is a maximizing matrix with the least possible number k of nonzero rows, since that number is an integer in a finite range.

## 2. Its nonzero rows are linearly independent

This conclusion needs only continuity for attainment and nonnegative homogeneity for the objective. Suppose a minimal-active maximizer had a relation

    sum_(i active) a_i X_i=0

with a not identically zero. The coefficients have both signs: the rows are nonnegative and nonzero, so a nontrivial all-one-sign combination cannot vanish. For t in a closed interval about zero for which 1+t a_i>=0, replace each active row by (1+t a_i)X_i. Column sums remain unchanged and all entries remain nonnegative. The objective is exactly

    H_c(X)+t sum_i a_i c_i phi(X_i).

Both signs of small t are feasible. Maximality forces the coefficient of t to vanish. At a finite endpoint of the feasible interval at least one formerly nonzero row vanishes, while no new row appears, and the objective stays maximal. This contradicts minimality of k. Therefore the active rows are linearly independent.

## 3. Cancellation of one row variation by row scalings

Let X be a weighted global maximizer, let row r be fully positive, and let v belong to the linear span of the active rows. Choose coefficients a_i with

    v+sum_i a_i X_i=0.

For sufficiently small positive and negative t, the following matrix is feasible:

    X_r(t)=(1+t a_r)X_r+t v,
    X_i(t)=(1+t a_i)X_i for active i!=r,

with zero rows unchanged. Positivity of X_r handles its additional perturbation; the other rows retain their supports. The displayed relation preserves every column sum exactly.

Assume phi is differentiable at X_r and has a second directional expansion along v with coefficient Q(v). Set s=t/(1+t a_r). Homogeneity gives the exact identity

    phi(X_r(t))=(1+t a_r)phi(X_r+s v).

The global objective's linear term must vanish by maximality in both signs. Subtracting that term leaves

    H_c(X(t))-H_c(X)
      =c_r(1+t a_r)[phi(X_r+s v)-phi(X_r)-s Dphi(X_r)[v]].

Thus a positive coefficient Q(v) contradicts maximality whenever c_r>0. In the C2 case, Q(v)=v^T Hess(phi)(X_r)v. More generally a strict two-sided increase over the tangent along v gives the same contradiction, without assuming C2.

In particular, at a minimal-active maximizing matrix every full differentiable row has nonpositive second variation along every direction in the active-row span for which that expansion exists. If k=m and a full row has any positive direction, it is excluded, because the active rows span the whole coordinate space.

If the row Hessian has a positive definite subspace of dimension p and k+p>m, elementary linear algebra forces a nonzero vector in its intersection with the k-dimensional active-row span, again contradicting maximality. This dimension count is conditional on the actual Hessian signature and differentiability at the row; it does not silently establish those facts for a knot or repeated entry.

The lemma provides an exact rank reduction and a concrete test for future full-row classifications. It is not a claim that every maximizing matrix has full rank or that all proper capacity cuts are twice differentiable.
